# Introduction {auto-animate="true"}
\hypertarget{sec:intro}{}

\Large\bfseries\textcolor{darknavy}{Functional Data Analysis:}

\small\normalfont
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
  % -------- Left: bullets (come one by one) ----------
  \begin{column}{0.62\textwidth}
  {\small\normalfont
  \begin{itemize}
    \item<1-> Functional data are observations that vary continuously over a domain (like time, space, or wavelength) and are often visualized as curves, trajectories, or functions rather than isolated points.
    \item<2-> These data are often recorded at discrete time points or grid locations, even though they originate from continuous processes in areas like engineering, finance, environmental science, and healthcare.
    \item<3-> Functional Data Analysis (FDA) is a statistical framework that treats these observations as realizations of smooth underlying functions, allowing for more accurate modeling and interpretation of continuous processes.
  \end{itemize}}
  \end{column}

  % -------- Right: image ----------
  \begin{column}{0.38\textwidth}
    % show from the first bullet onward
    \only<1->{\centering\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{images/FDA1.png}}
  \end{column}
\end{columns}
